body:
Thanks for the report. Can you try the development version? 

- The [Releases](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/tag/nightly) page has pre-built archives for Linux/Windows/macOS. 
- Check `:version` to confirm that you are using the latest version.

I can reproduce it with `NVIM v0.5.0-502-g2f818eb9e`, both appimage and building from AUR:
NVIM v0.5.0-502-g2f818eb9e
Build type: RelWithDebInfo
LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3

No, it only crashes with the lower-case letter for Alt-р: 
```
р
```
Here it is: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Er_(Cyrillic)
@OVlasiuk I've tried several Russian keyboard layouts in my Linux Box, but none of them get the Р(U+420) typed in Alt-p. What are the keyboard settings in your environment?

For me anything like `setxkbmap ua` or `setxkbmap ru` or `setxkbmap bg` works. 
Switch to either layout, then find the key that emits р (that is lowercase, so U+0440). If your keyboard has qwerty layout, it is probably mapped to the "h" key (for the first two, it is on "," for `bg`, IIRC). Then, press `alt-р` in the insert mode.

`setxkbmap -query` gives
```
rules:      evdev
model:      pc105
layout:     ua
```

@OVlasiuk Thanks. After` setxkbmap ru`, I confirmed that the phenomenon is reproduced by inputting `alt+h(key)` (`alt+р (U+440)`) in Xface Terminal with `Disable all menu access keys (such as Alt+f)` checked.

From backtrace this looks similar to #11788. The problem is that `add_char2buf()` requires `MB_MAXBYTES` + 1 bytes, but passes a buffer of only 6 bytes as shown below. I don't understand all the processing, so I can't decide if I should change 6 to `MB_MAXBYTES`+1 or not. Can someone who is familiar with the process here take a look at it?

body:
I am unable to reproduce this on kitty with a russian layout (might be that my WM catches the mapping). How do you map the symbol to its producing key on linux ? i've looked at setxkbmap-1.3.2/share/X11/xkb/symbols/ru but could only find  `Cyrillic_pe,`.
@erw7 once again, thanks for providing a patch, hoping to merge soon.

> I am unable to reproduce this on kitty with a russian layout (might be that my WM catches the mapping).

@teto I think the easiest way to reproduce this phenomenon is to `:call nvim_input('<M-'.nr2char(0x440).'>')`. If xterm is installed, I think it can be reproduced by typing `alt+р (U+440)`  in nvim on xterm started with `xterm -xrm 'xterm*VT100.metaSendsEscape: true'`. I think the input for `alt+р (U+440)` is Russian keyboard layout and the actual keys are `alt+r` or `alt+h`. I couldn't find a setting in kitty that would send an alt key to the application. However, if you set `map alt+h send_text all \x1b\u0440` in kitty.conf, you can reproduce the phenomenon with `alt+h` input regardless of the keyboard layout.
